correctness.rationale: The exact projection equation has degree 2m and gives the sign deck symmetry for both d parities. Counting inversion pairs of nontrivial (d-1)-roots of unity proves precisely m-1 distinct simple critical points of p_d; equality of critical-value moduli forces the same inversion pair, and their magnitudes exceed 2, making p_d(0) regular. Connected Morse monodromy gives S_m. A single local sign transposition above v=2, conjugated by S_m, generates all m independent flips, proving full C2 wreath S_m; local critical value types and infinity follow. Geometric irreducibility of the n>=2 Fermat generic fiber makes base change preserve this group. Point-stabilizer normalizer yields exactly C2 deck transformations. An exact algebraic checker confirms critical-value properties for d=4..25 but is not treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with Miura--Taki 2026 §§1--5 and Takahashi 2016 §§1--4 finds the 24 Fermat-quartic centers and the degree-five plane-curve D4 case already known, respectively, but neither contains the all-degree C2 wreath S_m formula with the root-of-unity Morse proof and complete finite branching portrait. Focused searches in the published-finding index and primary-literature discovery did not locate a mathematically dominating all-degree statement. This is a qualified self-review, not a proof that no earlier equivalent theorem exists; a cited unpublished Fermat projective-lifting manuscript is a real residual risk.
residual_risks: The Fermat projective-lifting manuscript cited by Miura--Taki as in preparation was not inspectable; it may contain relevant group computations.
Classical composition-monodromy literature may contain the all-d binomial polynomial Morse property under another name.

value.rationale: Miura--Taki identify the 24 non-Galois centers on a natural Fermat quartic K3 surface but give only order-two deck transformations, leaving their degree-four normal closures unspecified. The theorem upgrades the picture to complete dihedral monodromy there and obtains a sharp family-wide (all d,n>=2) normal-closure group and branch-cycle type distribution, with group order growing from D4 to 2^m m!. It clarifies a structural difference between the visible quasi-Galois automorphism group and the full monodromy, and isolates a uniform cyclotomic Morse lemma. Known d=5 curve instances are explicitly acknowledged, not used to claim novelty by dimension alone.
